_readme: Known symbols for ES1's PLAYFLIC.EXE (ES1PLAYFLIC): confirmed address -> meaning mappings, applied to the ES1Recon Ghidra project by ES2ApplySymbolNames.java.
Addresses are offsets into the flat X-32 image (Herculan/docs/es1/formats/x32-executable.md#the-image).
Schema, confidence rules and run order: tools/ghidra_scripts/README.md, 'Known symbols'.
Entries are in address order. tools/scripts/es2_naming.py insert and edit keep it, and check that it holds.

entries.name: Flic_Main
entries.description: (argc, argv): READFLIC's main. With argc < 2 prints the usage text and returns. The flic's name is argv[1]; each later argument starting with - or / is looked up by its second character in the 12-dword table 000158e0 (S s Z z D d B b C c Q q) and its handler taken from the table 0x30 on: S atoi(rest) into the speed override local, Z atoi into 000155f8, D 000155f0 = 1 and a call to 00004d48, B atoi into 000155fc, C atoi into 00015600, Q 000155f4 = 0; others passed over. Then Machine_Open (00001e20)(00024a60); when it answers >= 0, Flic_Open (000030f0)(name, flic local); when that answers >= 0, a non-zero override into the flic's +0x10, Flic_CenterOnScreen (00000510), Flic_Play (00003530) and Flic_Close (000031a4); Machine_Close (00002104) after an open machine. An answer < 0 other than -10 prints READFLIC had troubles with the name and Flic_ErrorText (000036a8).

entries.name: Flic_CenterOnScreen
entries.description: (screen, flic): the flic's x origin +0x8c = (Screen_Width (000018e0) - the header's width +8) / 2 and y origin +0x90 = (Screen_Height (000018f0) - the header's height +0xa) / 2, signed division.

entries.name: Preload_Open
entries.description: (chunk load, buffer size, flic): allocates the 0x28-byte preload record with +0 the header's file size, a buffer of the lesser of the buffer size and the file size at +4, and a 0x7fff-byte frame buffer at +8; seeks the flic's file (+0x80) to frame 1 (+0x50) and reads the buffer's size into it; +0xc = 0, +0x10, +0x14 and +0x18 = that size, +0x1c the chunk load. Returns the record, or 0 when an allocation fails (freeing what it took).

entries.name: Preload_Close
entries.description: (record): frees the preload record's two buffers (+4, +8) and zeroes +4, +0xc, +0x10, +0x14 and +0x18. The record itself is not freed.

entries.name: Profile_GetString
entries.description: (file, size, buffer, default, key, section): ES1DBSIM's Profile_GetString (000511a4) by es2_naming diff, with two differences: a key's value, after its first =, passes through 000017d4 before it is copied, and an empty one is passed over for a later line of the key in the section, then the default. The calls are the C library's strcat (00005484) and strchr (000053dc) and the same load, save and compare steps.

entries.name: Bios_SetVideoMode
entries.description: (mode): INT 10h function 0 with AL the mode, through 000073be. Returns 1.

entries.name: Bios_GetVideoMode
entries.description: (): INT 10h function 0x0f; returns AL, the current video mode.

entries.name: Screen_OpenMode13
entries.description: (screen): zeroes the 0x14-byte screen record, saves Bios_GetVideoMode (00001824) at +0xc, sets mode 0x13 with Bios_SetVideoMode (000017f8) and, when the mode then reads back as 0x13, sets +0x10 = 1 (open), +4 = 320, +8 = 200 and +0 the pixels' address for 0xa0000; returns 0. Otherwise sets the saved mode back and returns -7.

entries.name: Screen_Close
entries.description: (screen): when open (+0x10), sets the saved video mode (+0xc) back with Bios_SetVideoMode (000017f8) and zeroes the 0x14-byte record.

entries.name: Screen_Width
entries.description: (screen): returns +4, the width.

entries.name: Screen_Height
entries.description: (screen): returns +8, the height.

entries.name: Vga_SetDac8
entries.description: (count, rgb, first): sends count entries from first to the VGA DAC (port 3c8 the index, 3c9 the channels), each 8-bit channel shifted right by 2, and copies the 8-bit bytes into the DAC copy at 00024d4e.

entries.name: Vga_SetDac6
entries.description: (count, rgb, first): as Vga_SetDac8 (00001af0) with the channels sent as they are, 6-bit.

entries.name: Clock_Open
entries.description: (clock): +0 = 0x1234dc, 1,193,180 ticks a second, and the tick count 00025052 = 0. Returns 0.

entries.name: Clock_Read
entries.description: (): latches the 8253's counter 0 (port 43 then two reads of port 40) and returns the clock in its ticks from the tick count 00025052, the reload 00016c7c and the counter halved.

entries.name: Key_Poll
entries.description: (key): Bios_Keyboard (00006f3c)(1); with no key waiting returns 0, otherwise stores the word at key +0 and +1 and returns 1. The key stays in the buffer.

entries.name: Key_Read
entries.description: (key): Bios_Keyboard (00006f3c)(0), which takes the key out of the buffer; stores it at key +0 and +1 and returns its low byte.

entries.name: Machine_Open
entries.description: (machine): zeroes the 0x27f-byte machine, opens the keyboard (+0x18, 00001c98, 0), Clock_Open (00001c1c)(+0x14) and Screen_OpenMode13 (00001844)(+0); a failure of any returns its answer. Then reads the SoundFX and Music drivers and ports and the drivers' path from RESOURCE.CFG, detects or forces the sound card at +0x1b and opens the drivers into +0x1a5 with SoundSys_Open (00005f08); when they open returns 0. When the card is not found or the drivers do not open it answers 0 too, leaving the screen open.

entries.name: Machine_Close
entries.description: (machine): Screen_Close (000018b8)(+0), SoundSys_Close (00006110)(+0x1a5) on the sound, and the clock's and keyboard's closes, which do nothing.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeSync
entries.description: (machine, sync 0002566c, data): chunk type 0x18's handler. Data: the sync (0xd clock, 0xe sound), a flag, the sound's number, a zero adjust in ms. For 0xe with 000155f4 (sound, cleared by -Q) at 0 returns at once. 0xd: start (sync +8) = Clock_Read (00001c40). 0xe: sync +0xc = the number, start = DigiSample_Position (00008814)'s position of the sound of that number in the list 00015c2c, or 0. Another sync value leaves the start. With the flag set adds the zero adjust, (adjust * rate) / 1000 unsigned; then, flag or not, -Z's 000155f8 the same way, but with a signed division for a sync other than 0xd; the rate is the clock's (0xd) or 11,025. Sync +0 = the chunk's sync, +4 (the frame count) = 1. With the flag set waits for the start, on the clock or on the sound (none of that number: no wait), a waiting key read with Key_Read (00001ce8) ending the wait.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeSound
entries.description: (sound system machine+0x1a5, flic, data): chunk type 0x15's handler; nothing while 000155f4 (cleared by -Q) is 0. Data: an operation, a number, a NUL-ended name. 0: RESOURCE.CFG [FlicPlayer] pathFlic (default .\) through Profile_GetString (00000e58), sprintf %s%s with the name; a 0x84-byte node from malloc (00004038), +0 the number, DigiSample_Init (0000860c)(node+4, number, SoundSys_DigiDriver (000061a8)), DigiSample_Load (000086c8)(node+4, path); on success DigiSample_SetVolume (000087d0)(node+4, 0x7fff), node+0x80 = the head 00015c2c and the head = the node. 1: DigiSample_Start (000088cc) of the first node of the number in 00015c2c; 2: DigiSample_Stop (00008918). 3: the same load from [FlicPlay] pathFlic into a 0x9c-byte node through 00008934 and 000089e4, linked at +0x98 into 00015c30; 4 and 5: 00008aac and 00008afc on the first node of the number in 00015c30. Debug messages under -D (000155f0).

entries.name: Flic_FadeStep
entries.description: (screen): a step of a kind-9 palette fade. The remaining count 00025662 goes down by 1; k = that count, or with the direction 00025666 = 7, the steps 0002565e less it. Each channel of the 256 entries is P + (C - P) * k / steps, P the palette copy at 00025056, C the color at 00025668, signed and truncated, into 0002535a, which Vga_SetDac8 (00001af0) sends whole.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeFade
entries.description: (screen, flic, data): chunk type 0x16's handler. Data: the direction (6 from the color, 7 to it), the kind (8 at once, 9 a step a frame), the steps n (0 as 1) and the color 0x0RGB, each nibble shifted up by 4. Kind 8 sends P + (C - P) * k / n for k = n down to 1 then P (6), or k = 1 up to n (7), back to back with Vga_SetDac8 (00001af0), and zeroes 0002565e and 00025662. Kind 9 stores the color at 00025668, the direction at 00025666, n at 0002565e and 00025662, runs Flic_FadeStep (000027a8) and adds 1 back to 00025662. Another direction or kind does nothing.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeChunk14
entries.description: (screen, flic, data): chunk type 0x14's handler. Calls Flic_DecodeCopyDelta (00003e19)(screen's pixels (+0) + flic +0x90 * screen's stride (+4) + flic +0x8c, data, the stride): the frame's origin, the y offset at flic +0x90 and the x offset at +0x8c, on the screen buffer.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeColorPackets
entries.description: (setter, screen, flic, data): a uint16 packet count, then each packet a byte of entries to skip, a count byte (0 for 256) and three bytes an entry. While no fade runs (00025662 = 0) calls setter(count, rgb, first, screen); always copies the packet into the palette copy 00025056 at its first entry.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeColor256
entries.description: (screen, flic, data): chunk type 4, COLOR_256: Flic_DecodeColorPackets (00002c54) with Vga_SetDac8 (00001af0).

entries.name: Flic_DecodeColor64
entries.description: (screen, flic, data): chunk type 0xb, COLOR_64: Flic_DecodeColorPackets (00002c54) with Vga_SetDac6 (00001b68).

entries.name: Flic_DecodeBlack
entries.description: (screen, flic): chunk type 0xd, BLACK: for each of the header's rows from the origin (+0x8c, +0x90), width / 2 words of 0 with 00001a84 and, for an odd width, the last pixel 0 with 00001900.

entries.name: Flic_Open
entries.description: (name, flic): zeroes the 0x98-byte flic record, opens the file into +0x80 (error -5) and reads the 128-byte header into +0 (-6 when short); +0x88 = the name. Magic 0xaf12 (.FLC): seeks to frame 1 (+0x50), returns 0. Magic 0xaf11 (.FLI): +0x50 = 0x80 and the speed +0x10 = +0x10 * 1000 / 70, returns 0. Another magic closes the file and returns -3.

entries.name: Flic_Close
entries.description: (flic): closes the file at +0x80 and zeroes the 0x98-byte record.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeFrame
entries.description: (screen, frame, flic): walks the frame chunk's subchunks, as many as its +6 word, the first at +0x10, each advanced by its own +0 dword size, and dispatches each by its +4 type word on (screen, flic, the subchunk's data at +6): 4 Flic_DecodeColor256, 7 FUN_00002ecc, 0xb Flic_DecodeColor64, 0xc FUN_00002df4, 0xd Flic_DecodeBlack, 0xf FUN_00002d38, 0x10 FUN_00003094, 0x14 Flic_DecodeChunk14 (00002c1c), 0x15 Flic_DecodeSound (on screen + 0x1a5 rather than the screen), 0x16 Flic_DecodeFade, 0x17 FUN_00002b64, 0x18 Flic_DecodeSync (on 0002566c rather than the flic); any other type is passed over. Returns 0.

entries.name: Flic_NextFrame
entries.description: (screen, flic): reads the next chunk with FUN_000007c0(local, flic); with none returns -4. A chunk of type 0xf1fa whose +0 size is not 4 goes to Flic_DecodeFrame (000031d0)(screen, chunk, flic), whose answer it returns; a frame of size 4 returns EBX as it stood; any other type returns -4. Calls FUN_00000690(flic) before returning on every path but the first.

entries.name: Flic_FrameDue
entries.description: (clock, speed ms, sync): the frame's due time, (speed * rate) / 1000 unsigned, times the sync's frame count (+4), plus its start (+8); the rate is the clock's (+0) for the sync 0xd and 11,025 otherwise. The first call off the clock also keeps (speed * the clock's rate) / 1000 in 00015c34 and that times the double 0.05 into 000248f8 through the C library's __LNGDBL@ (00008075), __DMUL@ (00007ea8) and __DBLLNG@ (00008110) and Clock_Read (00001c40, into 000248fc).

entries.name: Flic_WaitFrame
entries.description: (machine, due, sync): on the clock (sync 0xd) loops until Clock_Read (00001c40) reaches due, unsigned, checking Key_Poll (00001ca4) first each pass; a key is read with Key_Read (00001ce8) and returns -10. Otherwise waits the same way on DigiSample_Position (00008814)'s position of the sound whose number is the sync's +0xc in the list 00015c2c, and with no such sound returns at once. Returns 0.

entries.name: Flic_FindFrame2
entries.description: (flic): seeks the file to frame 1 (+0x50) and reads the 16-byte frame header; +0x54 = frame 1's offset plus its size. Returns the read's error, or 0.

entries.name: Flic_Play
entries.description: (machine, flic): Preload_Open (00000554)(00015600, 000155fc, flic) into flic +0x94; the sync 0002566c = 0xd with its start 00025674 = Clock_Read (00001c40) and frame count 00025670 = 1. Then for each of the header's frames (+6): Flic_FadeStep (000027a8) while 00025662 is not 0; Flic_NextFrame (00003348), whose error ends the loop; Flic_FrameDue (000033a8)(clock, speed +0x10, sync); the frame count + 1; Flic_WaitFrame (00003440), whose -10 ends it. Then Preload_Close (00000658); returns the last Flic_NextFrame answer.

entries.name: Flic_ErrorText
entries.description: (error): Success for 0 and above; for -5 and -6 0000858d's text for 00015e73; -1 to -10 from the table 00015c08; any other Unknown error.

entries.name: Flic_DecodeCopyDelta
entries.description: (dest, data, stride), ending in a plain RET: decodes a 0x14 picture chunk in place onto dest. Reads the dword command count, then each command's opcode, the low 3 bits of its first byte, through the jump table 00003c7c: 0 skip (word >> 3 pixels), 1 literal (word >> 3 bytes after the word), and 2-7 copies from dest itself at a signed offset (2: byte >> 3, n byte 1; 3: byte 1, n byte >> 3; 4 and 5: byte >> 3 less or plus stride, n byte 1; 6: word >> 3, n word 2; 7: word 2, n word >> 3), each copy as REP MOVSW of n / 2 words, then one MOVSB when n is odd. The loop counts the low 16 bits of the count.

entries.name: DigiInitBlock_Init
entries.description: (block, rate): the digital driver's init block: +0 = 0x1000 (the buffer), +0xc = 1 (the driver allocates it), +0x10 = the rate, the rest 0. SoundSys_Open (00005f08) passes 11,025.

entries.name: SoundSys_Open
entries.description: (sound system machine+0x1a5, card machine+0x1b, MIDI device, MIDI port, drivers' path): device 0xa002 and port 0x388 for 0; the path .\ default for null; clears the state +0xb8 and the far pointers at +0xc9, +0xcf, +0xd5; DigiInitBlock_Init (00005c48)(+0, 11,025), 00005c90 and 00005cd8 fill the blocks at +0x88 and +0x5c; port at +0xac; 000036fc(0x13, 0), 0000aa8f and 00009e10 on the path. HmiMidi_InitDriver (0000a03f)(device, +0xac, +0x5c, handle out +0xb9); on success device 0xa005 into +0xbd, else +0xb9 = -1; on success 00005db4(system, path), failing as 0xe; else +0xbd = -1. With error 0 (00018928): 0000c2ee(0) and the state 1. Otherwise 00005d0c, 0000a4a0(handle, 1) for each handle >= 0, 000037c0(0), 0000a02d and 0000aafc. Returns the state.

entries.name: SoundSys_Close
entries.description: (sound system): with the state +0xb8 set, 0000a597 on the handles +0xb9 and +0xbd, 00005d0c, 0000a4a0(handle, 1) on +0xbd and +0xb9, 000037c0(0), 0000aafc, 0000a02d, and the state cleared; nothing otherwise.

entries.name: SoundSys_DigiDriver
entries.description: (sound system): returns the dword +0xb9, the handle HmiMidi_InitDriver (0000a03f) gives the [Music] device, which Flic_DecodeSound (000023ec) hands its samples as their driver.

entries.name: SoundSys_SetDriverPath
entries.description: (card, path): copies the path, with its zero, to +0x7c (a zero byte there for null), and clears the bytes +0x17c and +0x17d.

entries.name: SoundSys_EndDetect
entries.description: (card): with +0x17c set, 0000c65f and +0x17c cleared.

entries.name: SoundSys_Detect
entries.description: (card): 0000c4a5 on the path +0x7c (which opens hmidet.386), then 0000ca49(card, card+0x6c) and 0000ce31(card+0x6c), each while the error 00018928 stays 0. With 0: +0x17d and +0x17c set to 1 and returns 1; otherwise 0000c65f and returns 0.

entries.name: SoundSys_ForceCard
entries.description: (card, port, DMA, IRQ, device): +0x6c the port, +0x74 the DMA channel, +0x70 the IRQ, +0x64 the device: Machine_Open's card from RESOURCE.CFG's [SoundFX] when its Driver# is not 0.

entries.name: Bios_Keyboard
entries.description: (function): INT 16h with AH the function. Function 1 returns 0 with no key waiting and the key word, or -1 for a word of 0, with one; function 0 returns the key read.

entries.name: DigiSample_Init
entries.description: (object, id, driver): HmiDigi_StartSample's start block with no data: +0x78 the driver, +0x7c (the loaded state) 0, +0x18 the id, +0x28 0x100, +0x10 2, +0x14 0x7fff, +0x40 0x8000, the far pointer +0, +8, +0xc and the other fields to +0x64 zero. Returns 1. Leaves +0x74 alone.

entries.name: DigiSample_Free
entries.description: (object): by the loaded state +0x7c: 1, frees the data with 0000c494 (the far pointer +0); 2, clears the far pointer; then the state 0.

entries.name: DigiSample_Load
entries.description: (object, path): DigiSample_Free (0000868c), +0xc (the loop count) 0, File_LoadWhole (0000c3f8)(path, &+8) into the far pointer +0. With the size +8 not 0 sets the state +0x7c to 1 and returns 1; otherwise 0.

entries.name: DigiSample_SetVolume
entries.description: (object, volume): +0x14 the volume, and bit 1 of the byte +0x29 (flag 0x100) set.

entries.name: DigiSample_Position
entries.description: (object): the bytes of the sample played. HmiDigi_GetBytesProcessed (00009543)(driver +0x78, voice +0x74), plus the distance forward, 1 to 0x1000, from HmiDigi_GetDmaPosition (000093fd)(driver) to the DMA transfer's place 0x1000 - n in the driver's buffer, n one more than the count read twice from the channel's count port (00016c50[00016c70[driver]], the flip-flop at port 0xc cleared first), doubled for a port above 7; the distance halved when the dword 000169f0 + driver * 0x6c is not 0.

entries.name: DigiSample_Start
entries.description: (object): HmiDigi_StartSample (0000d229)(driver +0x78, object); its voice into +0x74 and returns 1, or for -1 +0x74 = 0 and returns 0.

entries.name: DigiSample_Stop
entries.description: (object): HmiDigi_StopSample (0000d4cf)(driver +0x78, voice +0x74).

entries.name: HmiDigi_GetDmaPosition
entries.description: (driver): the dword the far pointer at 0001698c + driver * 6 points at; DigiSample_Position (00008814) takes it as the driver's place in its DMA buffer.

entries.name: HmiDigi_GetBytesProcessed
entries.description: (driver, voice): the voice record's (far pointer at 000165ac + driver * 0xc0 + voice * 6) dword +0x4c while bit 0x8000 of its word +0x30 is set; 0 otherwise. HmiDigi_StartSample (0000d229) zeroes +0x4c.

entries.name: HmiMidi_InitDriver
entries.description: (device, port block, block, handle out) of the HMI library: ES1DBSIM's HmiMidi_InitDriver (00071076) by es2_naming diff, with two differences: device 0xa008 calls the driver as 0xa005 does, and device 0xa003's branch first copies six far pointers into the driver's table; the rest differs in addresses.

entries.name: File_LoadWhole
entries.description: (path, size out): filesize (00005300) of the path, that many bytes from malloc (00004038), the file opened (00005133, mode 0), read whole (000050fc) and closed (0000526e); returns the far pointer to the bytes and stores the size. A file that does not open prints FAIL: '%s' no exist through printf (0000429a), stores size 0 and returns 0, leaving the block allocated.

entries.name: HmiDigi_StartSample
entries.description: (driver, block) of the HMI library: ES1DBSIM's HmiDigi_StartSample (0006dad9), identical after normalisation by es2_naming diff. Returns 0 when the dword 00016578[driver] is above 0xe105, and -1 when all 32 voices (far pointers at 000165ac + driver * 0xc0) have bit 0x8000 of their word +0x30 set; otherwise copies the block into the first free voice record, sets its word +0x30 to the block's flags | 0xa000, zeroes +0x4c, and returns the voice.

entries.name: HmiDigi_StopSample
entries.description: (driver, voice) of the HMI library: ES1DBSIM's HmiDigi_StopSample (0006dd7f), identical after normalisation by es2_naming diff.
